title: How do you connect two tables in Hibernate/JPA, and which annotations (@OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @JoinColumn, mappedBy) do you use?
shortTitle: How do you connect two tables with @OneToMany?
keyPoints: @ManyToOne on the child entity is the owning side that controls the foreign key column in the database
@OneToMany(mappedBy) on the parent entity is the inverse side used for navigation only
@JoinColumn(name = "account_id") specifies which FK column in the child table references the parent
mappedBy = "account" tells JPA that the Trade.account field owns the relationship
Always synchronize both sides with helper methods: addTrade() sets both the list and the FK
Setting only the inverse side (account.getTrades().add(trade)) does NOT set the FK in the database
Unidirectional @OneToMany without @ManyToOne creates an unnecessary join table – avoid it

s1_definition.oneliner: @ManyToOne on the child with @JoinColumn is the owning side that controls the FK; @OneToMany(mappedBy) on the parent is the inverse side for navigation only – always set both sides with helper methods.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **@ManyToOne** – placed on the child entity (Trade). Points to the parent (Account). This is the owning side that controls the FK column.
- **@JoinColumn** – specifies the FK column name in the child table: `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")`.
- **@OneToMany(mappedBy)** – placed on the parent entity (Account). Creates the inverse side for navigation. `mappedBy = "account"` tells JPA the Trade.account field owns the relationship.
- **Owning side** – the side that controls SQL generation. Only changes to the owning side are persisted.
- **Helper methods** – `addTrade()` and `removeTrade()` synchronize both sides of the bidirectional relationship.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, Account (parent) has many Trades (children). In the database, the trades table has an `account_id` FK column pointing to accounts. In Java, Trade has `@ManyToOne Account account` (the trade knows which account it belongs to – owning side). Account has `@OneToMany List<Trade> trades` (the account can see its trades – inverse side). `mappedBy` tells JPA: "Trade.account is the real owner – I am just the mirror."

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Bidirectional @OneToMany / @ManyToOne:

  accounts table              trades table
  ┌───────────────┐          ┌───────────────────┐
  │ account_id PK │─────────┤ trade_id    PK   │
  │ holder_name   │          │ symbol           │
  │ balance       │    ┌────┤ account_id  FK   │
  └───────────────┘    │    │ amount           │
                         │    └───────────────────┘
                         │
  Java mapping:          │
  Account (INVERSE)      │    Trade (OWNING)
  @OneToMany(mappedBy)   │    @ManyToOne + @JoinColumn
  List<Trade> trades  ───┘    Account account

  Helper method flow:
  account.addTrade(trade)
    │
    ├── trades.add(trade)      (inverse side)
    └── trade.setAccount(this)  (owning side → FK set!)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
JPA connects two tables using `@ManyToOne` on the child entity (owning side, controls the FK column) and `@OneToMany(mappedBy)` on the parent entity (inverse side, navigation only). `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")` specifies the FK column. `mappedBy = "account"` tells JPA that the `Trade.account` field owns the relationship. JPA reads only the owning side for SQL generation.

At National Bank of India, Trade has `@ManyToOne(fetch = LAZY) Account account` with `@JoinColumn(name = "account_id")`. Account has `@OneToMany(mappedBy = "account", cascade = ALL, orphanRemoval = true)`. The `addTrade()` helper synchronizes both sides: it adds to the list (inverse) and calls `trade.setAccount(this)` (owning). Without the helper, the FK column is NULL because JPA only reads the owning side.

Three relationship patterns exist: unidirectional `@ManyToOne` (simplest, child knows parent), bidirectional `@ManyToOne` + `@OneToMany(mappedBy)` (both navigate, standard), and unidirectional `@OneToMany` without `@ManyToOne` (creates an unnecessary join table, avoid it). Always use bidirectional with helper methods for production code, and always set `fetch = FetchType.LAZY` on `@ManyToOne` to prevent N+1 queries.

Remember one sentence: the child's @ManyToOne with @JoinColumn owns the FK, the parent's @OneToMany(mappedBy) is just a mirror, and helper methods must set both sides.
